title: Instagram broke the link my customers live on. I had a week to fix it.
text: Medium Instagram broke the link my customers live on. I had a week to fix it. | by Thomas Melto | Sep, 2026 | Medium Sitemap Open in app Sign up Sign in Medium Logo Get app Write Search Sign up Sign in Member-only story Startup Instagram Entrepreneurship Product Management Creator Economy Instagram broke the link my customers live on. I had a week to fix it. On 18 March 2026, Meta changed one default in the Instagram app. By the end of the day, the agencies on my platform had lost most of their revenue. Thomas Melto 6 min read · Sep 24, 2026 -- Listen Share Press enter or click to view image in full size The same link, opened from an Instagram story. The visitor was logged in to this platform in Safari. Here, they are not. On 18 March 2026, Instagram stopped handing links to the visitor’s browser. A tap on a bio link that used to open Safari or Chrome started opening Instagram’s own in-app browser instead, and stayed there. No announcement, no changelog, no email to developers. One day the handoff worked, the next day it did not. I run LinkScale, a link tool for creators and the agencies that manage them. Most of our users send Instagram traffic to platforms where the visitor has to be logged in to pay. The browser handoff was the reason a tap turned into a subscription. When it disappeared, our product did not break. Our customers’ funnel did. We found out the way you never want to: early that morning, support messages started arriving all at once, all saying a version of the same thing, the link opens but nobody converts anymore. Then we opened the accounts we use for our own demos and tests, tapped our own links, and watched them stay inside Instagram. It was not one client. It was everyone. The change looked cosmetic… -- -- Written by Thomas Melto 2 followers · 25 following Founder of LinkScale.
